handoff.purpose: Define constants, dataclass, and symbol extraction utilities for graph brief generation.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET_CHARS
symbols.note: Default character budget for a whole brief, set to 12,000.

symbols.name: DEEP_EDGE_MARK
symbols.note: String marker for edges that exist only inside function bodies, set to '*'.

symbols.name: ARTEFACT_ROOTS
symbols.note: Tuple of path prefixes that are artefacts and must never appear in a brief.

symbols.name: _HEADER_RESERVE
symbols.note: Characters reserved for the header, set to 700.

symbols.name: _is_artefact
symbols.note: Returns True if the given relative path starts with any of ARTEFACT_ROOTS.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Dataclass holding a rendered brief plus its source facts: text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, provenance.

symbols.note: Property returning True if any dropped values are truthy.

claims.text: the agents never see the graph. No provider module references ``structcore``, ``build_index``, ``typegraph`` or ``forest``.

claims.text: The entire context a write lane gets is ``read_inlined_context`` -- raw file bytes and nothing else.
claims.why: No write lane or read_inlined_context function is defined in this chunk.

claims.text: So a model asked to write ``tests/test_shift.py`` had no way to know that the class is ``Shift`` and not ``ShiftManager``, that linting lives at ``daedalus.gui.lint`` and not ``daedalus.linting``, or that the vault is ``daedalus.wiki.vault`` and not ``daedalus.wiki_vault``. It guessed, plausibly, three times, and a syntax gate passed all three.
claims.why: No evidence of that test file or syntax gate in this chunk.

claims.text: All three of those hallucinations are answered by ~6.5k characters of text that the index can already produce.
claims.why: No index or measurement data in this chunk.

claims.text: the graph was built, the graph was measured, and the graph was never connected to the consumer.
claims.why: No evidence of graph building or measurement in this chunk.

claims.text: Function-body edges are marked ``*``: 202 of 526 internal edges in this repo are only visible there, so a brief built from top-level imports alone would present ~60% of the graph as the whole of it.
claims.why: No repo-wide import analysis is present; the constant DEEP_EDGE_MARK is defined as '*' but the numbers 202 and 526 are not verifiable.

claims.text: Layers 2 and 3 degrade cleanly: the type and document layers of the index are behind flags, and when they are off those sections are omitted rather than faked.
claims.why: No flag definitions or layer rendering code is in this chunk.

claims.text: What is never omitted silently is a TRUNCATION -- if the budget cuts the brief, the brief says what it dropped.
claims.why: No budget allocation or truncation reporting code is in this chunk.

claims.text: This is a DERIVED artefact. It is regenerated, never edited, and a model must not cite it as evidence about behaviour -- it describes shape, not semantics.
claims.why: No enforcement or generation logic is in this chunk.

claims.text: Default character budget for a whole brief. Sized from measurement, not taste: the full symbol layer for the ``daedalus/`` package is 6,479 characters, so a 1-hop brief around a handful of files fits comfortably and the budget only bites on a genuinely wide change.
claims.why: The constant is defined as 12,000, but the claim about measurement and daedalus package size cannot be checked without the package content.

claims.text: Marks an edge that exists ONLY inside a function body. See the module docstring: this is the 38% of the import graph that naive tooling misses.
claims.why: The module docstring says 202 of 526 (≈38.4%), but the constant's docstring says 38%. The two values are consistent, but the claim is about the module docstring; the module docstring says 202 of 526 (≈38.4%), not exactly 38%. However, the constant docstring claims 'this is the 38%', which is approximately correct (38.4% ≈ 38%), but the module docstring does not explicitly say 38%. The claim is 'this is the 38%' – it is a rounding, but not exact. Given the module docstring says '202 of 526', which is 38.4%, calling it 38% is a minor inaccuracy. Verdict: broken (inaccurate rounding).

claims.text: Path prefixes that are ARTEFACTS, not the project, and must never appear in a brief.
claims.why: The constant is defined as a tuple of path prefixes, and the function _is_artefact uses it to filter. The docstring claim matches the code.

claims.text: Both entries are measured, not defensive: ... runs/ ... build/ ...
claims.why: The claim that these are measured is not verifiable from the code; no measurement data is present.

claims.text: runs/ -- the first brief built for ``daedalus/shift.py`` listed ``runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py`` as a graph neighbour and printed its symbols. That file is the DESTROYED artefact kept as evidence: a test module that overwrote the real one. Showing it to a model asked to edit ``shift.py`` teaches it precisely the substitution the write gate now refuses -- the brief would have been arguing for the bug.
claims.why: No evidence of that specific run or write gate in this chunk.

claims.text: build/ -- holds 142 stale copies of the package. Every naive sweep double-counts them, and a brief that lists a symbol twice from two versions of one file is worse than one that omits it.
claims.why: No directory listing or count is present.

claims.text: Characters reserved for the header, which is composed after the layers are budgeted. Generous on purpose: overshooting the reserve wastes a few hundred characters, while under-reserving silently pushes the brief over the budget a caller sized its prompt against.
claims.why: No budget allocation or header composition code is present.

observations.what: The module docstring makes extensive claims about the graph and model behaviour that are not verifiable in this chunk.
The constant DEEP_EDGE_MARK is defined as '*' and the docstring claims it marks function-body edges; the module docstring also mentions '*' for that purpose. The code is consistent.

The constant ARTEFACT_ROOTS includes four prefixes: 'runs/', 'build/', 'dist/', '.captures/'. The docstring only describes 'runs/' and 'build/' in detail but the tuple also contains 'dist/' and '.captures/'.

The function _is_artefact is defined and used to filter paths based on ARTEFACT_ROOTS. The docstring claim that artefacts 'must never appear in a brief' is enforced by this function, but the rendering code that calls it is not in this chunk.

The GraphBrief dataclass includes fields text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, and provenance. Properties char_count and truncated are defined. No methods for rendering or populating these fields are present.
The function _sig extracts parameter names from ast function nodes, but only handles posonlyargs and args; it does not handle vararg, kwonlyargs, kw_defaults, or kwarg. This may be incomplete.
Several symbols listed in __all__ (graph_brief, render_brief, file_symbols) are not defined in this chunk. They will be defined in subsequent chunks.
